objective: Review the latest commit (HEAD) on release/0.3.1/chore/bump-version in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-bump: a shared Windows-aware timeout for tests that start the CLI, and a stall diagnostic in the pi project-flag test.
scope: Run git -C /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-bump show HEAD. Files: packages/runtime/tests/fixtures.ts (PROCESS_TIMEOUT_MS, 120 s on win32 and 30 s elsewhere), pipe.test.ts, version.test.ts, pi extension.test.ts, pi.test.ts, session-context.test.ts (CHILD_DEADLINE_MS and PIPE_GRACE_MS: kills a stalled child and fails with its arguments and partial output) and claude hooks.test.ts.

Purpose: the Windows runner intermittently stalls cold CLI starts; the maintainer asked to raise the timeout. Check that no assertion or test body weakened, that the diagnostic cannot fail a healthy run on Linux or macOS (13.5 s per child against a 30 s test) and kills its child cleanly, and that the bun fmt re-indentation hides no change.
constraints: Do not check out other commits in any checkout and make no edits.
Report in under 300 words; mark each finding blocking or non-blocking with file and line.

criteria.text: No assertion is weakened and the diagnostic cannot fail a healthy run
The shared constant is used consistently by every changed test

result:
result: HEAD ac863f85 is mergeable on these criteria. I found no blockers.

The built-in `/code-review` ran as the built-in. Its six findings all cite files outside this commit (design-core, web-design SKILL, `docs/attributions.md`, and others), so they belong to another range. I rejected them as out of scope and none concerns this change. The built-in also reported it could not run tests; I ran them myself.

Findings:
**Assertions unchanged (non-blocking, verified).** I diffed with `git show HEAD -w`. The `bun fmt` re-indentation hides no change. In `extension.test.ts`, `pipe.test.ts` and `version.test.ts` the only differences are the wrapper (`test(name, fn, PROCESS_TIMEOUT_MS)`) and the import. `hooks.test.ts` and `pi.test.ts` change only the timeout value.
**Shared constant used everywhere in the changed files (verified).** `PROCESS_TIMEOUT_MS` is imported and applied in all seven files. No literal `30_000` remains in them. `fixtures.ts:19` is 120 s on win32 and 30 s elsewhere.
**Diagnostic is safe on a healthy run.** Only `session-context.test.ts` (around lines 195-225) has it. `Bun.spawn({timeout: CHILD_DEADLINE_MS})` kills only a child still running at 13.5 s, and `signalCode` is non-null only after that kill, so the `throw` cannot fire on a normal exit. The pipe-grace race returns the `<pipe open after exit>` placeholder only if a pipe is still open 2 s after the child exits. That case hung before this change.
**Kill is clean (Bun built-in, not run).** The built-in `timeout` option kills the child, and `child.exited` then resolves, so `Promise.all` settles. A grandchild holding a pipe is covered by the grace race. I did not run a real stall.
**Leftover timer (non-blocking, `session-context.test.ts` ~line 211).** `Bun.sleep(PIPE_GRACE_MS)` stays pending up to 2 s after a healthy read wins the race. It is harmless.
**Windows timeouts not shared (non-blocking, outside this diff).** `cli.test.ts`, `vcs*.test.ts`, `migrate.test.ts` and `state-mode.test.ts` still use `60_000` on win32. `brief.test.ts` uses a flat `30_000` with no win32 branch.

evidence:
No assertion is weakened and the diagnostic cannot fail a healthy run: `git show HEAD -w` shows only wrapper and timeout changes. The diagnostic throws only when `signalCode !== null`. `bun test` on pipe, version, session-context, extension and pi: exit 0, 285 pass, 0 fail. `bun fmt --check`, `bun lint` and `bun check` all clean.
The shared constant is used consistently by every changed test: all seven files import `PROCESS_TIMEOUT_MS` from `packages/runtime/tests/fixtures.ts:19`, with no `30_000` literal left in them.
findings: no blockers, three non-blocking notes above, and the built-in review's six findings rejected as outside this range.
